title: LUXFER ENTERS INTO AGREEMENT TO BE ACQUIRED FOR $17.37 PER SHARE IN ALL-CASH TRANSACTION
summary: LUXFER ENTERS INTO AGREEMENT TO BE ACQUIRED IN ALL-CASH TRANSACTION
body_text: LUXFER ENTERS INTO AGREEMENT TO BE ACQUIRED FOR $17.37 PER SHARE IN ALL-CASH TRANSACTION 27 July 2026 RIVERSIDE, CA, July 27, 2026 -- Luxfer Holdings PLC (NYSE: LXFR), a global industrial company innovating niche applications in materials engineering, today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by affiliates of Wynnchurch Capital, L.P. (“Wynnchurch”) in an all-cash transaction. Transaction Overview Under the terms of the agreement, which has been unanimously approved by the directors in attendance at a meeting of Luxfer’s Board of Directors, Luxfer shareholders will receive $17.37 per ordinary share in cash. The purchase price represents: ~30.7% premium to Luxfer’s closing share price of $13.29 on April 28, 2026, the last trading day prior to Luxfer’s first quarter 2026 earnings release, when Luxfer announced an active strategic review. Management Comments “Over the past several years, we have strengthened Luxfer through disciplined operational execution, enhanced our positions in attractive end markets and invested in differentiated technologies. These actions have improved profitability, created a stronger business and positioned Luxfer for long-term success. We believe this transaction delivers compelling value for our shareholders while providing an excellent opportunity for our employees, customers and partners to continue building on Luxfer’s legacy of innovation.” Andy Butcher , Chief Executive Officer - Luxfer “Luxfer is a differentiated advanced materials company with leading technical capabilities, deep metallurgical expertise and mission-critical products serving attractive aerospace, defense and demanding industrial end markets. We have tremendous respect for the business and management team and look forward to supporting the Company with long-term capital, operational resources and sector expertise.” Greg Gleason , Managing Partner – Wynnchurch “We see meaningful opportunities to invest in innovation, operational excellence, automation, capacity expansion and commercial growth across both of Luxfer’s segments. We also believe the Company is well positioned to pursue complementary acquisitions that can broaden its capabilities, product portfolio and geographic reach.” Brian Riordan , Managing Director – Wynnchurch Transaction Information The transaction is currently expected to be completed prior to the end of 2026, subject to approval of Luxfer shareholders, receipt of regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. The transaction is not subject to financing conditions. Until the transaction is completed, Luxfer will, subject to the terms of the definitive agreement, continue to operate in the ordinary course of business, serving its customers, supporting its employees and executing its strategic priorities. Upon completion of the transaction, Luxfer will become a privately held company, and its ordinary shares will no longer be listed on the New York Stock Exchange. Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. is acting as exclusive financial advisor to Luxfer, and Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson LLP is acting as legal advisor to Luxfer. Lazard is acting as exclusive financial advisor to Wynnchurch, and Kirkland & Ellis LLP is acting as legal advisor to Wynnchurch. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Announcement Luxfer expects to report its second quarter 2026 financial results on Tuesday, July 28, 2026, after the closing of the New York Stock Exchange. In light of the pending transaction, Luxfer will not host an investor conference call or webcast to discuss its second quarter 2026 financial results. About Luxfer Luxfer is a global industrial company innovating niche applications in materials engineering. Using its broad array of proprietary technologies, Luxfer focuses on value creation, customer satisfaction, and demanding applications where technical know-how and manufacturing expertise combine to deliver a superior product. Luxfer’s high-performance materials, components, and high-pressure gas containment devices are used in defense and emergency response, clean energy, healthcare, transportation, and specialty industrial applications. For more information, please visit www.luxfer.com. Luxfer is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and its ordinary shares trade under the symbol LXFR. About Wynnchurch Capital, L.P. (“Wynnchurch”) Wynnchurch Capital, L.P. is a leading middle-market private equity investment firm that has been investing in industrial businesses for more than 25 years. Wynnchurch is currently investing out of its sixth private equity fund and manages approximately $9.1 billion of assets under management. The firm’s strategy is to partner with middle-market companies that possess the potential for substantial growth and profit improvement. Wynnchurch specializes in recapitalizations, growth capital, management buyouts, corporate carve-outs, and restructurings. Recent exits include the pending sale of FloWorks to Ferguson Enterprises Inc. (NYSE: FERG) in a transaction valued at approximately $1.6 billion and sale of Labrie Environmental Group to Hiab Corporation (Nasdaq Helsinki: HIAB) in a transaction valued at approximately $1.035 billion. Recent investments include MSHS Pacific Power Group, Sterno, NABRICO Marine Products, Charter Industries, and Astro Shapes. For more information, please visit: www.wynnchurch.com or follow on LinkedIn. Additional Information In connection with the proposed transaction between Luxfer and Wynnchurch, Luxfer will file with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) a proxy statement on Schedule 14A. Additionally, Luxfer may file other relevant materials with the SEC in connection with the proposed transaction. Investors and securityholders of Luxfer are urged to read the proxy statement (which will include notices convening the scheme meeting and the general meeting of Luxfer’s shareholders to be convened in connection with the scheme of arrangement, and an explanatory statement in respect of the scheme of arrangement of Luxfer, in accordance with the requirements of the U.K. Companies Act 2006) and any other relevant materials filed or that will be filed with the SEC, as well as any amendments or supplements to these materials and documents incorporated by reference therein, carefully and in their entirety when they become available because they contain or will contain important information about the proposed transaction and related matters. The definitive version of the proxy statement will be mailed or otherwise made available to Luxfer's securityholders. Investors and securityholders will be able to obtain a copy of the proxy statement (when it is available) as well as other filings containing information about the proposed transaction that are filed by Luxfer with the SEC, free of charge on EDGAR at www.sec.gov, on the investor relations page of Luxfer's website at https://www.luxfer.com/investors, or by contacting Luxfer's investor relations department at Investor.Relations@Luxfer.com. Participants in the Solicitation Luxfer and its directors and executive officers may be deemed to be participants in the solicitation of proxies from Luxfer’s shareholders in respect of the transaction. Information about Luxfer’s directors and executive officers is set forth in the proxy statement for Luxfer’s 2026 Annual General Meeting, which was filed with the SEC on April 30, 2026. Other information regarding the participants in the proxy solicitation and a description of their interests will be contained in the proxy statement and other relevant materials to be filed with the SEC in respect of the proposed transaction when they become available. Forward-Looking Statements This communication includes “forward-looking statements” within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, including with respect to the proposed acquisition of Luxfer, and readers are cautioned not to place undue reliance on such statements. Such forward-looking statements include, but are not limited to, the ability of Wynnchurch and Luxfer to complete the transactions contemplated by the transaction agreement, including statements about the transaction, statements about the expected timetable for completing the transaction, Luxfer’s beliefs and expectations and statements about the benefits sought to be achieved in the proposed acquisition, and the potential effects of the acquisition on Luxfer. These statements are based upon the current beliefs and expectations of Luxfer's management and are subject to significant risks and uncertainties. There can be no guarantees that the conditions to the closing of the proposed transaction will be satisfied on the expected timetable or at all. If underlying assumptions prove inaccurate or risks or uncertainties materialize, actual results may differ materially from those set forth in the forward-looking statements. Risks and uncertainties include, but are not limited to, uncertainties as to the timing of the proposed transaction; the risk that competing offers or acquisition proposals will be made; the possibility that various conditions to the consummation of the proposed transaction contained in the transaction agreement may not be satisfied or waived (including, but not limited to, the failure to obtain shareholder approval and the failure to obtain the sanction of the High Court of Justice in England and Wales); the occurrence of any event, change or other circumstances that could give rise to the termination of the transaction agreement; the effects of disruption from the transactions contemplated by the transaction agreement and the impact of the announcement and pendency of the transactions on Luxfer’s business, including its ability to retain and hire key personnel and maintain relationships with customers; the risk that any announcements relating to the transaction could have adverse effects on the market price of Luxfer’s ordinary shares; the risk of any unexpected costs or expenses resulting from the transaction; the risk that shareholder litigation in connection with the transaction may result in significant costs of defense, indemnification and liability; and other risks related to Luxfer’s business. Luxfer undertakes no obligation to publicly update any forward-looking statement, whether as a result of new information, future events or otherwise, except to the extent required by law. Additional factors that could cause results to differ materially from those described in the forward-looking statements can be found in Luxfer’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 and Luxfer’s other filings with the SEC. title: How to Compare Managed WiFi Vendors for Apartments
summary: Learn how to compare managed WiFi vendors for apartments with this guide covering network design, NOI impact, and resident support benchmarks.
body_text: Choosing the right managed WiFi vendor can shape how your apartment community performs for years. The wrong choice locks you into outdated technology and support headaches; the right one turns connectivity into a genuine competitive advantage. If you're a property owner or asset manager evaluating managed WiFi solutions for your multifamily portfolio, this guide walks you through the criteria that matter—from network design and resident support benchmarks to the NOI impact you can expect from a well-executed deployment. Elauwit Connection delivers managed WiFi solutions built specifically for apartment communities, bringing enterprise-grade network infrastructure with 24/7 resident support. Throughout this guide, you'll find practical frameworks you can apply immediately, whether you're comparing vendors for a single property or standardizing connectivity across a portfolio of communities. Key Takeaways: How to Compare Managed WiFi Vendors for Apartments Network architecture and technology standards directly determine your residents' daily experience with connectivity. 24/7 resident support with fast response times reduces the burden on your property management team significantly. NOI impact varies widely between vendors based on ownership models, revenue sharing, and capital requirements. Elauwit Connection offers flexible ownership options including Network-as-a-Service with zero upfront capital for property owners. Retrofit versus new construction deployments require different evaluation criteria and vendor capabilities. What Is Managed WiFi for Apartment Communities? Managed WiFi is a professionally designed, installed, and maintained wireless network that delivers consistent coverage across your entire property. Unlike the retail model where each resident contacts their own ISP and installs their own router, managed WiFi treats connectivity as building infrastructure—similar to water or electricity. The provider handles network design, deployment, monitoring, and resident support. Your residents get online by setting a password when they move in. No technician appointments. No competing routers creating signal interference between units. This approach has shifted from a premium amenity to an expected standard. According to the National Multifamily Housing Council , over 85% of apartment residents now rank reliable internet as their top amenity priority—ahead of fitness centers, pools, and package lockers. Why Does Managed WiFi Vendor Selection Matter for Property Owners? Your managed WiFi vendor becomes a long-term partner, not a one-time purchase. Most contracts span five to ten years, during which time your residents will judge your property based partly on connectivity quality. A poor selection means dealing with resident complaints your team cannot fix. The vendor you choose also determines your financial outcomes. Some vendors require significant upfront capital for infrastructure. Others offer zero-cost deployment with ongoing service fees. The ownership model affects who controls the network, who handles upgrades, and how revenue flows back to you. Beyond economics, vendor capability determines whether your network can support future demands. Smart building systems, access control, package lockers, and energy management all depend on reliable connectivity. The wrong infrastructure today becomes a limitation tomorrow. How to Evaluate Network Design and Technology Standards Network design separates professional managed WiFi from basic bulk internet arrangements. You're looking for an enterprise-grade approach that handles the unique challenges of multifamily housing: high device density, building construction materials that block signals, and residents with widely varying usage patterns. What WiFi Technology Standards Should You Require? The current standard for new deployments is WiFi 6, which handles more devices per access point and performs better in congested environments. WiFi 6E extends into the 6 GHz band, offering additional channels with minimal interference. WiFi 7 is emerging as the next generation, offering even faster speeds and improved reliability. Ask prospective vendors specifically what technology they deploy. Some vendors install equipment that was current five years ago. That hardware cannot deliver the speeds modern residents expect from streaming, gaming, and remote work. A vendor installing WiFi 5 equipment today is setting you up for early obsolescence. How Does Access Point Placement Affect Coverage? Proper coverage requires access points placed strategically throughout units and common areas. Consumer routers in each unit create competing signals that degrade performance for everyone. Enterprise systems use coordinated channel management across all access points, eliminating the interference that plagues dense housing. Look for vendors who conduct site surveys before quoting. Buildings with concrete walls, metal structures, or unusual layouts need customized approaches. A vendor who quotes without understanding your building's specific characteristics is guessing. What Speed Commitments Should You Expect? Be cautious of "up to" speed claims. A promise of "up to 1 Gbps" often delivers significantly less under real-world conditions with multiple devices connected. More meaningful commitments specify minimum speeds during peak usage times. Gigabit-capable infrastructure has become the baseline expectation for new installations. Leading vendors now discuss multi-gigabit capabilities that accommodate where technology is heading, not just where it stands today. How to Assess Resident Support Benchmarks and Capabilities Resident support quality directly affects your property team's workload and your residents' satisfaction. When WiFi problems occur—and they will—someone needs to resolve them quickly. That responsibility either falls on your staff or on your vendor's support team. Why Does 24/7 Support Matter for Apartment WiFi? Connectivity issues do not follow business hours. A resident working from home cannot wait until Monday for a fix when their connection drops Friday evening. Look for vendors offering genuine 24/7 support with live representatives, not just after-hours voicemail or chatbots. Response time metrics matter. Elauwit Connection maintains an average support call answer time of approximately 34 seconds, ensuring residents reach a real person quickly when issues arise. Ask prospective vendors for their average response times and hold them accountable. How Should Vendors Handle Resident Onboarding? Move-in day sets the tone for a resident's entire experience. The best managed WiFi systems allow residents to get online immediately—no technician visits, no waiting periods. Residents create their account, set a password, and connect their devices. Ask how the vendor handles the transition when residents move out. Network access should deactivate promptly, and the next resident should be able to activate service just as quickly. Smooth transitions reduce friction and eliminate security gaps. What Reporting and Visibility Should Property Teams Receive? You should not be blindsided by resident complaints. Quality vendors offer dashboards showing network health, usage patterns, and any emerging issues. This visibility lets your team understand what residents experience without becoming technical experts. Proactive monitoring means the vendor identifies and resolves many issues before residents even notice. Ask how the vendor monitors network performance and what their escalation process looks like when problems occur. Understanding the NOI Impact of Different Vendor Models Managed WiFi can become a meaningful contributor to your Net Operating Income. However, the financial impact varies dramatically based on the model you choose and how the vendor structures their services. What Ownership Models Exist for Managed WiFi? Several models exist, each with different implications for your balance sheet and ongoing operations: Owner-owned infrastructure: You fund the network build, own the equipment, and retain full control. The vendor operates and maintains the network under a service agreement. Higher upfront capital, but you capture more of the ongoing value. Vendor-owned infrastructure: The vendor funds and owns the equipment. You pay ongoing service fees, typically per unit per month. Lower upfront investment, but you give up some long-term flexibility. Network-as-a-Service (NaaS): A fully managed model where the vendor handles everything for a predictable monthly fee. Elauwit Connection offers Network-as-a-Service with zero upfront capital for the core build, making it accessible for properties that prefer to preserve cash for other priorities. How Can Managed WiFi Generate Revenue for Property Owners? Property owners typically generate revenue through bulk arrangements where connectivity costs are included in rent or as a technology fee. The spread between what you pay the vendor and what residents pay creates monthly income. Some vendors share upgrade revenue when residents choose premium speed tiers. Others offer revenue sharing on the base service. The specifics matter: ask exactly how revenue flows and what documentation you'll receive. What NOI Improvements Are Realistic? Industry benchmarks suggest managed WiFi can generate meaningful ancillary income per unit monthly, which flows directly to NOI. The exact figures depend on your market, property type and the vendor's economic model. Beyond direct revenue, well-implemented managed WiFi supports higher rent positioning and improved retention. Properties with reliable connectivity report lower turnover rates compared to properties where residents must coordinate their own internet service. Evaluating Vendors for Retrofit Versus New Construction Projects Your deployment scenario affects which vendors can serve you well. A vendor skilled at new construction may lack the expertise for occupied properties, and vice versa. What Special Considerations Apply to Retrofit Deployments? Retrofitting an occupied community means working around current residents. The vendor needs a detailed cutover plan that minimizes disruption. Residents can't lose connectivity during installation, and the transition from old infrastructure to new must be managed carefully. Elauwit Connection offers retrofit and network takeover services designed specifically for occupied communities. This includes assessment of existing infrastructure, cutover planning and resident communication support throughout the transition. Ask how the vendor has handled similar retrofits. References from comparable properties matter more than generic marketing claims. What Should You Evaluate for New Construction Deployments? New construction offers the advantage of designing connectivity into the building from day one. The vendor should coordinate with your general contractor and low-voltage partners during the construction phase. Look for vendors who can deliver documentation and as-built records for your ownership and onsite teams. Proper documentation guarantees future maintenance and upgrades can proceed smoothly. Timeline coordination matters. A vendor who can't keep pace with construction schedules creates delays that ripple through your entire project. How Do Portfolio Requirements Differ from Single-Property Deployments? Multi-property operators need consistency across their portfolio. Standardized infrastructure, unified support processes, and consolidated reporting become essential at scale. Elauwit Connection supports portfolio-level consistency for multi-property operators, so your residents receive the same quality experience regardless of which community they live in. This standardization simplifies training for your teams and creates predictable outcomes. Critical Contract Terms and Red Flags to Watch For The contract determines your relationship for years. Certain terms deserve careful attention, and certain patterns should raise concerns. What Contract Length Is Appropriate for Managed WiFi? Most managed WiFi contracts run five to 10 years. This duration reflects the significant infrastructure investment involved. However, longer terms should come with protections: technology refresh commitments, performance guarantees and clear escalation procedures. Be wary of contracts that lock you into specific equipment without provisions for upgrades. Technology will advance during your contract term, and your agreement should accommodate that reality. What Performance Guarantees Should You Require? Look for specific, measurable commitments rather than vague promises. Uptime guarantees with meaningful penalties demonstrate vendor confidence. Speed commitments during peak hours show realistic expectations. Service level agreements should specify response times for different issue severities. A complete network outage needs faster attention than a single resident's connection problem. What Are Common Red Flags in Vendor Proposals? Watch for vendors who quote without site surveys, promise unrealistic speeds or can't explain their support model clearly. A vendor who avoids answering direct questions about technology, staffing or financial terms may be hiding limitations. References matter. Ask for contacts at properties similar to yours and actually call them. A vendor reluctant to share references likely has something to hide. Building a Vendor Evaluation Scorecard Comparing vendors requires a structured approach. Different criteria matter differently depending on your priorities, but a scorecard helps promote consistent evaluation. What Network Design Criteria Should You Score? Evaluate each vendor on technology standards (WiFi generation, access point quality), coverage approach (site survey process, access point density) and speed commitments (minimum guaranteed speeds, peak performance). Weight these according to how connectivity-dependent your residents are. What Operational Criteria Should You Score? Score support availability (hours, response times, escalation paths), resident onboarding experience (move-in process, activation speed) and monitoring capabilities (dashboards, proactive alerts, reporting). These factors determine day-to-day experience. What Financial Criteria Should You Score? Evaluate ownership model fit, capital requirements, ongoing costs and revenue potential. Consider the total cost of ownership over the contract term, not just initial pricing. What Strategic Criteria Should You Score? Consider vendor stability and experience, compatibility with your future plans (smart building systems, access control) and flexibility for portfolio growth. A vendor who fits today but can't scale with you creates problems tomorrow. Making Your Managed WiFi Vendor Decision Comparing managed WiFi vendors requires balancing technical capability, operational excellence and financial fit. The right vendor becomes a partner who enhances your property's value and simplifies your operations. The wrong vendor creates ongoing headaches and disappointed residents. Focus your evaluation on the criteria that matter most for your specific situation. A Class A property in a competitive market may prioritize cutting-edge technology. A value-add acquisition may prioritize retrofit capability and economics. Your priorities should shape your evaluation. Take the time to conduct thorough due diligence. Site visits, reference checks and detailed proposal reviews reveal far more than marketing materials. The effort you invest in selection pays dividends throughout a multi-year relationship. When you're ready to evaluate managed WiFi vendors for your apartment community, consider Elauwit Connection . With nearly two decades of expertise in technology strategy and infrastructure deployment, Elauwit Connection delivers the combination of enterprise-grade network design, exceptional resident support and flexible ownership models that multifamily property owners need. FAQs about How to Compare Managed WiFi Vendors for Apartments What is the difference between managed WiFi and bulk internet? Managed WiFi includes professional network design, installation, monitoring and resident support as an integrated service. Bulk internet typically means discounted service purchased in volume, but residents may still install individual routers and contact the ISP for support. The managed approach eliminates competing signals between units and gives property teams visibility into network performance. How long do managed WiFi contracts typically last? Most contracts run five to 10 years to account for infrastructure investment. Shorter terms may be available but often come with higher costs. Elauwit Connection offers flexible contract structures that align with your capital planning timeline. Review termination provisions carefully before signing any long-term agreement. Can I retrofit managed WiFi into an occupied property? Yes, many vendors specialize in retrofit deployments. The key is choosing a vendor with experience managing transitions in occupied communities. Elauwit Connection handles retrofit projects with minimal disruption, including cutover planning and resident communication support. Ask for references from similar retrofit projects before selecting your vendor. What speeds should managed WiFi deliver to residents? Gigabit-capable infrastructure has become the baseline for new installations. More important than headline speeds is consistent performance during peak usage times when many residents stream, game and work simultaneously. Require minimum speed guarantees rather than accepting "up to" claims that rarely reflect reality. How does managed WiFi affect my property's NOI? Managed WiFi generates NOI through bulk service arrangements where the spread between vendor costs and resident charges creates monthly income. Additional benefits include reduced turnover costs and the ability to position your property competitively in the market. Elauwit Connection supports property economics with flexible models designed to protect and grow your NOI. What support should residents receive with managed WiFi? Quality vendors offer 24/7 resident support with live representatives, not just business-hours assistance. Elauwit Connection maintains approximately 34-second average answer times, so residents reach help quickly when connectivity issues arise. Fast support response protects your property's reputation and keeps problems from escalating.
